machine.notes: Cloud container. 4 visible vCPUs but ~1.5-2 cores of real throughput (4 parallel CPU-bound processes run 2.5x slower each); other agents were running FFmpeg/tests in the same container during measurement, so wall times vary by up to ~60% between identical runs. Ranges over repeated runs are reported, not single numbers.
machine.hw_note: none works in this container (no GPU / VAAPI device); the NEXUS_HWENC=1 path was not exercised on real hardware

timeline.description: synthetic 62.0 s programme, 1280x720 @30 fps, 8 clips: 7 video clips of 8.0 s cut from 9 s lavfi sources (testsrc2 1920x1080, mandelbrot, life, cellauto at 1280x720; H.264 crf 22 + AAC of an amplitude-modulated 180 Hz sine as speech-like audio) and one 7.5 s colour clip with a title overlay; 0.5 s crossfades into clips 3, 6 and 8; 21 burned caption cues over the whole programme (legacy classic style); procedural 'calm' music bed at volume 0.4 with ducking. The life/cellauto sources are high-entropy noise (~37 Mbit/s at crf 20), so every render is dominated by x264 encode time: a pessimistic case.
timeline.script: bench.py in the agent scratchpad (not committed); builds the timeline with nexus.timeline / nexus.audio.music

what_changed: clips render as video-only head/body/tail parts + PCM audio, cache-missing clips in parallel (ThreadPoolExecutor, workers=cpu//2, -threads cpu//workers)
transitions are short xfade pieces (tail+head) instead of an xfade chain re-encoding the whole programme
captions and programme overlays are burned per piece at programme time (setpts shift for libass); burned pieces are a second cache level, so caption edits re-burn only the pieces they touch

intermediate parts that are always re-encoded (transition heads/tails, bodies that get captions) use a mezzanine encode (x264 ultrafast crf 14): ~2x faster to encode, ~3x faster to decode on this content
final pass is a pure stream copy (concat demuxer) of video pieces + finished audio; no full-programme video re-encode

audio: sample-exact programme audio from PCM parts; loudness measured with ebur128 (cheaper than loudnorm's 192 kHz analysis) and applied as the equivalent linear gain; mix + AAC encode run in parallel with the video pieces and are cached by input hash
draft=True: half resolution, x264 ultrafast crf 30, separate cache namespace (cache/segments_draft)
removed_or_not_helping: a first version without the mezzanine encode and with audio on the critical path was measured at 43-51 s cold (no better than baseline); kept only the changes above
parallelism alone helps little on this container: workers=1 cold 34-52 s vs workers=2 24-40 s (same machine, interleaved runs) for the final pipeline
honest_limits: cold renders encode most frames twice (mezzanine part + final burned piece) because captions cover the programme; the win comes from cheaper intermediates and removing two full-programme re-encodes
a timing edit that shifts later clips re-burns every later piece that carries captions or a progress bar (burned at programme time)
changing a transition's duration re-renders the two neighbouring clips from source (head/tail split points change)
